name: Methane Liquefaction Linde Cycle Three Stage
description: Pure methane vapour is compressed in three sequential stages with intercooling between each stage to bring the gas to high pressure. The high-pressure stream is then cooled to a cryogenic temperature before passing through an expander that reduces pressure and temperature further. The resulting two-phase stream is separated into vapour and liquid fractions in a gas-liquid separator, yielding liquid methane as product while the vapour fraction is recycled back to the compressor inlet.
prompt: Simulate a Linde cycle to liquefy methane gas. The gas is compressed and cooled in multiple stages, then expanded to produce a two-phase stream from which liquid methane is separated as product and the vapour fraction is recycled to the compressor inlet.
notes: Ground-truth reference: VAL_01_reference.json. Source DWSIM file: Methane_Liquefaction_Cycle.dwxmz. Property package corrected to Peng-Robinson (EOS appropriate for pure methane at high pressure; original DWSIM file used NRTL which is thermodynamically incorrect for a single-component hydrocarbon system). Unit tags inferred from flowsheet diagram: COMP-01/02/03 -> K-01/02/03; COOL-01/02/03 -> CO-01/02/03; EXP-01 -> EX-01; SEP-01 -> V-01; E-01 through E-08 -> HT-01 through HT-08 (heat exchangers acting as regenerative coolers/heaters in the cycle). T_out for K-01 taken from S-02 (127.43C = 400.58K); T_out for K-03 taken from S-06 (116.08C = 389.24K); T_out for CO-01/CO-02 from downstream stream values (6.85C = 279.95K); T_out for CO-03 from S-07 (-63.15C = 210.00K). S-08 vapor_fraction null (post-expander two-phase state not explicitly stated). S-09 vapor_fraction = 1.0 (vapour product); S-10 vapor_fraction = 0.0 (liquid product).

name: Heterogeneous Azeotropic Separation Pyridine Water Toluene
description: A pyridine-water mixture, which forms a homogeneous azeotrope, is fed into a two-column heterogeneous azeotropic distillation system with toluene added as an entrainer. The entrainer exploits a heterogeneous toluene-water azeotrope to drive liquid-liquid phase splitting in a decanter, allowing the organic and aqueous layers to be routed separately. High-purity pyridine is recovered as the bottoms of the first column, while high-purity water is recovered as the bottoms of the second column, and the toluene-rich overhead is recycled back to the first column.
prompt: Separate pyridine and water from their azeotropic mixture using toluene as an entrainer in a heterogeneous azeotropic distillation process. The toluene entrainer exploits a liquid-liquid phase split to break the azeotrope, recovering high-purity pyridine and high-purity water as separate products with toluene recycled.

name: Hydrodealkylation Toluene to Benzene SRK Recycle
description: Toluene and hydrogen feeds are mixed and heated to reaction temperature before entering a conversion reactor where toluene is dealkylated to produce benzene and methane. The hot reactor effluent is cooled and passed to a vapour-liquid separator, where the hydrogen- and methane-rich vapour is recycled back to the reactor feed while the liquid fraction is reheated and sent to a distillation column. The distillation column recovers high-purity benzene as distillate while toluene-rich bottoms are pumped and recycled to the reactor feed mixer.
prompt: Simulate the hydrodealkylation (HDA) of toluene to benzene using a hydrogen feed at high temperature. The reactor effluent contains benzene, unreacted toluene, hydrogen, methane, and biphenyl byproduct; after cooling and separation, the hydrogen and methane-rich vapour and the unconverted toluene liquid are both recycled to the reactor feed.

Toluene feed pressure given as 2E+5 Pa = 200000 Pa = 2.0 bar. All other streams at 2.35E+06 Pa.

name: Hydrogen Production Biogas Reforming WGS PSA
description: Biogas (methane and carbon dioxide) is compressed and mixed with steam before being fed to a steam methane reformer operating at high temperature, where methane is converted to syngas (carbon monoxide and hydrogen). The syngas is cooled and passed through a water-gas shift reactor that converts carbon monoxide and steam to additional hydrogen and carbon dioxide. The shifted gas is further cooled to condense water, which is knocked out in separators, before the dry hydrogen-rich gas is purified in a pressure swing adsorption unit to yield high-purity hydrogen product while a tail gas containing carbon dioxide and residual methane is rejected.
prompt: Produce pure hydrogen from a biogas feed of methane and carbon dioxide by steam methane reforming followed by water-gas shift reaction. Steam is mixed with the compressed biogas before the reformer; the shift reactor converts carbon monoxide and steam to hydrogen and carbon dioxide; water and carbon dioxide are then removed to yield a high-purity hydrogen product.
notes: Ground-truth reference: VAL_04_reference.json. Source DWSIM file: Hydrogen_production_from_biogas.dwxmz. Property package: Peng-Robinson (EOS appropriate for H2/CO/CH4/CO2/H2O at high pressure reforming conditions). 18 units: K-01 (biogas compressor), P-01 (water pump), MX-01/02 (feed mixers), HT-01 through HT-07 (heaters including reformer and WGS), CO-01/02 (coolers), V-01 through V-04 (separators/knock-out drums), SP-01 (splitter for PSA tail gas split). 17 streams: WATER, BIOGAS, S-01 through S-09, S-011, S-012, S-014 through S-017, H2. Composition normalisation applied to S-05: Water adjusted 0.641687 -> 0.642547 (sum was 0.99914, deficit 0.00086 added to dominant component Water).

name: Vinyl Chloride Production EDC Chlorination Pyrolysis
description: Ethylene and chlorine feeds are mixed and reacted in a direct chlorination reactor to produce ethylene dichloride, which is purified and fed to a pyrolysis furnace where it is cracked at high temperature to yield vinyl chloride and hydrogen chloride. The furnace effluent is quenched and condensed before entering an HCl distillation column that recovers pure hydrogen chloride overhead, while the bottoms are sent to a vinyl chloride column that separates high-purity vinyl chloride as distillate and recycles the unconverted ethylene dichloride bottoms back to the pyrolysis feed.
prompt: Produce vinyl chloride monomer and hydrogen chloride from ethylene and chlorine via the balanced process route. Ethylene and chlorine react to form 1,2-dichloroethane (EDC), which is thermally cracked to yield vinyl chloride and hydrogen chloride; the two products are separated into pure streams and unconverted EDC is recycled back to the cracking stage.
notes: Ground-truth reference: VAL_05_reference.json. Source DWSIM file: Vinyl_Chloride_Production.dwxmz. name: Natural Gas Dehydration TEG Absorption Regeneration
description: Wet natural gas containing water, acid gases, and light hydrocarbons is contacted with lean triethylene glycol in an absorber column where TEG selectively absorbs water from the gas stream, producing dry sales gas overhead and a water-rich TEG bottoms. The rich TEG is flashed, heated, and fed to a regenerator column where water and light hydrocarbons are stripped overhead as sour gas while high-purity lean TEG is recovered as bottoms. The regenerated TEG is cooled and pumped back to absorber pressure before being recycled to the top of the absorber.
prompt: Dehydrate a high-pressure natural gas stream containing methane, ethane, propane, isobutane, n-butane, isopentane, n-pentane, nitrogen, hydrogen sulfide, carbon dioxide, and water using triethylene glycol (TEG) absorption. The wet gas contacts lean TEG in an absorber to produce dry sales gas; the water-rich TEG is regenerated by heating and stripping, and the lean TEG is cooled, repressurised, and recycled to the absorber.
notes: Ground-truth reference: VAL_06_reference.json. Source DWSIM file: Drying_of_Natural_Gas_using_TEG.dwxmz. Property package not stated — Peng-Robinson inferred as standard for natural gas + glycol dehydration at high pressure. Sub-1E-7 molar fractions rounded to 0.000000.

name: Extractive Distillation CO2 Ethane EOR NGL Separation
description: A high-pressure gas feed containing carbon dioxide and ethane as the primary components, along with heavier hydrocarbons from propane to pentane, is separated using a two-column extractive distillation system with n-pentane as the entrainer. The first column removes the carbon dioxide-ethane azeotrope overhead while the heavier NGL components and entrainer leave as bottoms. The second column separates high-purity ethane as its overhead product while the entrainer-rich bottoms stream is recycled back to the first column.
prompt: Separate ethane from carbon dioxide in a high-pressure enhanced oil recovery (EOR) gas that also contains propane, isobutane, n-butane, isopentane, and n-pentane, using extractive distillation with n-pentane as the solvent. Recover a high-purity ethane overhead product and an NGL-rich liquid product, with the n-pentane solvent recycled.
notes: Ground-truth reference: VAL_07_reference.json. Source DWSIM file: Extractive_Distillation_CO2_Ethane_EOR.dwxmz. Property package stated as Peng-Robinson 78 — mapped to Peng-Robinson as closest supported string. name: Extractive Distillation Acetonitrile Isopropanol Water Ethylene Glycol
description: A ternary feed of acetonitrile, isopropanol and water, which forms multiple binary and ternary azeotropes, is separated using a two-stage extractive distillation system with ethylene glycol as the entrainer. The first column recovers high-purity acetonitrile as distillate at sub-atmospheric pressure, while the second column recovers isopropanol-rich distillate at atmospheric pressure. The combined bottoms from both extractive columns are sent to an entrainer recovery column where water leaves overhead and high-purity ethylene glycol is recovered as bottoms and recycled.
prompt: Separate a ternary feed of acetonitrile, isopropanol, and water — a system with multiple binary azeotropes — using a two-stage extractive distillation process with ethylene glycol as the solvent. Recover high-purity acetonitrile and high-purity isopropanol as separate overhead products, with water removed and the ethylene glycol solvent recovered and recycled.

name: Extractive Distillation Benzene Ethanol P-Xylene Solvent
description: A benzene-ethanol azeotropic feed is separated using a two-column extractive distillation system with p-xylene as the entrainer. In the first column the entrainer raises the relative volatility of benzene relative to ethanol, allowing high-purity ethanol to be recovered as distillate while benzene and p-xylene leave as bottoms. The bottoms are fed to a second column where nearly pure benzene is recovered as distillate and the p-xylene-rich bottoms are cooled and recycled back to the first column with a make-up stream to compensate for solvent losses.
prompt: Separate an equimolar benzene–ethanol azeotropic feed using extractive distillation with p-xylene as the solvent. Recover high-purity ethanol as the first column overhead and high-purity benzene as the second column overhead, with p-xylene recycled from the solvent recovery step and a make-up stream added to compensate for losses.

name: Syngas Production RLNG Steam Reforming Ammonia Plant
description: Re-gasified liquefied natural gas and steam are fed to a primary reformer where methane is converted to syngas via steam reforming reactions, followed by a secondary reformer where air injection provides nitrogen and additional combustion heat. The syngas then passes through high-temperature and low-temperature shift converters to maximise hydrogen yield by converting carbon monoxide, followed by a carbon dioxide absorber to remove CO2, and finally a methanator to eliminate trace carbon oxides, yielding a purified hydrogen and nitrogen rich syngas suitable for ammonia synthesis.
prompt: Produce a hydrogen and nitrogen-rich syngas for ammonia synthesis from regasified LNG (methane) and steam. Primary steam reforming converts methane to hydrogen and carbon monoxide; secondary reforming with an air feed introduces nitrogen and drives further conversion; high and low temperature shift reactors then convert carbon monoxide to additional hydrogen; carbon dioxide is absorbed and removed, and trace carbon oxides are eliminated by methanation.
